proposed_findings.title: Remote listing names can inject arbitrary path segments
preconditions: Hub `list_tree` returns an entry path containing extra `/` segments
proof: Remote listing data from `hub_client.list_tree(&prefix)` is trusted in `ensure_children_loaded`. For root listings, `rel_path = entry.path.clone()`. If `rel_path.find('/')` succeeds, the code creates a child directory named the prefix before `/` and stores `dir_full_path = format!("{}/{}", prefix, dir_name)`; otherwise it inserts `rel_path` and `entry.path` directly as name/full_path. No check ensures `entry.path` is a single direct child of `prefix`, so remote-controlled paths inject synthetic descendants and arbitrary full paths into the VFS.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Reject non-direct children; canonicalize and validate `entry.path` stays under `prefix` without extra segments.

proposed_findings.title: User-controlled rename paths sent to backend without component validation
preconditions: rename caller controls `newname` reaching backend-synced rename path
proof: `rename()` accepts user `newname` and only rejects OS junk, then `rename_validate()` builds `new_full_path` with `inode::child_path(&new_parent_entry.full_path, newname)`. `rename_remote()` forwards that path in `BatchOp::AddFile.path` for file renames and derived descendant paths for directory renames. No component validation rejects separators or special segments before `hub_client.batch_operations(&ops)`. Reachable on every writable rename, allowing backend operations on unintended remote paths.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Reject rename names containing path separators or invalid path components before building remote paths.

proposed_findings.title: Symlink target from caller is stored and returned unsanitized
preconditions: Caller can invoke `symlink` with chosen target bytes
proof: `VirtualFs::symlink` takes caller-controlled `target` and stores it verbatim in `entry.symlink_target` (`src/virtual_fs/mod.rs:1064`). `readlink` later returns that stored string unchanged. No validation, normalization, or policy check occurs on the target before crossing into VFS state. Impact: arbitrary symlink destinations are persisted and exposed by the VFS. Reachable through any successful `symlink` call.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Validate or reject unsafe symlink targets before storing; return error on disallowed targets.

proposed_findings.title: Untrusted args file controls mount configuration
preconditions: attacker can write shared `tmp_dir` volume args file
proof: Input originates from `tmp_dir/.volumes/*/args`, described as a shared emptyDir. `discover_pending()` reads each file with `read_to_string`, splits lines into tokens, and passes them directly to `MountArgs::try_parse_from`, then `run_mount()` uses the parsed `source` and `options` in `build()`. No check binds files to the CSI driver or validates ownership/source. Any writer to the shared directory can influence mount configuration for a launched mount.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Verify args file provenance before parsing, e.g. trusted ownership/path checks or authenticated driver-signed configs.

proposed_findings.title: Sidecar accepts SCM_RIGHTS fd from any socket peer
preconditions: Attacker can create or impersonate the configured Unix socket path
proof: Input origin: `connect_and_receive_fd` connects to `socket_path` from discovered volume state. Propagation: after `UnixStream::connect`, it calls `recvmsg`, accepts the first `SCM_RIGHTS` fd, wraps it with `OwnedFd::from_raw_fd`, and passes it to `mount_fuse`. Failing condition: no peer credential or identity check occurs on the connected Unix socket. Impact: sidecar trusts an fd from any socket peer. Reachability: direct on every mount setup.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Verify peer credentials after connect and reject peers not matching the expected CSI driver identity.

proposed_findings.title: NFS mount advertises unsupported direct I/O
preconditions: NFS mount started with `--direct-io`
proof: CLI input sets `options.direct_io` in `build`. `VirtualFs::new` receives `direct_io: options.direct_io && !is_nfs`, so NFS forcibly disables it. But `MountSetup` later stores `direct_io: options.direct_io` unchanged, after only logging it is ignored for NFS. This leaves setup state claiming direct I/O is enabled while the backing VFS has it disabled, so NFS advertises an unsupported mode and can misconfigure backend-specific mount behavior.

proposed_findings.title: unlink_one leaves directory parent link count unchanged
preconditions: `unlink_one` is called on a directory child
proof: `insert()` increments the parent directory's `nlink` for `InodeKind::Directory`, and `remove()`/`move_child()` decrement it when detaching directories. In `unlink_one()`, input `name` is resolved from `parent.children`, the child entry is removed, `path_to_inode` is deleted, and only the child inode's `nlink` is decremented. No branch adjusts `parent_entry.nlink` for directory children. This leaves parent metadata inconsistent and reachable whenever directory unlink uses `unlink_one`.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: When unlinking a directory child, decrement the parent directory's `nlink` alongside removing the child entry.

proposed_findings.title: move_child can create duplicate child names in destination
preconditions: destination parent already has a child with the new name
proof: Caller-controlled `new_parent`/`new_name` reach `move_child`, which removes the old entry then unconditionally `push`es `DirChild { ino, name: new_name }` into `new_parent.children`. Unlike `insert`, no duplicate-name/path check occurs. If `new_parent` already contains `new_name`, `lookup_child` returns the first match while both entries remain, violating unique child-name expectations and leaving ambiguous directory state. Reachable via any rename or cross-parent move using `move_child`.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Before attaching, reject or replace an existing `new_parent` child with `new_name`.

proposed_findings.title: remove_orphan can leave stale parent child entry
preconditions: inode has nlink 0 and parent still lists it
proof: `unlink_one` leaves the inode in `inodes` with `nlink` decremented to 0, while removing only the named `DirChild`. `remove_orphan` later deletes just `inodes[ino]` and `path_to_inode[full_path]` (`src/virtual_fs/inode.rs:466`) without touching `entry.parent.children`. This creates a stale parent->child edge, violating table consistency. Reachable whenever an orphaned inode is removed after any remaining parent reference persists.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Make `remove_orphan` delegate to `remove`, or also prune `entry.parent.children` before deletion.

proposed_findings.title: Prefix cancel drops sibling delete paths
preconditions: queued deletes include sibling paths sharing a string prefix
proof: `cancel_delete_prefix` accepts a caller-controlled path prefix and filters `pending_deletes` with `!p.starts_with(prefix)` in `src/virtual_fs/flush.rs:102`. A prefix like `dir` also matches sibling paths such as `dir2/file`. Those unrelated delete entries are removed before `flush_pending_deletes` batches them, so reachable queued remote deletions for sibling paths are silently skipped.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: match whole path components, not raw string prefixes

proposed_findings.title: PID file deletion follows untrusted environment path
preconditions: Attacker controls daemon process environment variables
proof: `DaemonGuard::from_env()` reads `HF_MOUNT_DAEMON_PID_FILE` directly into `pid_file` from the environment. `Drop` later always calls `std::fs::remove_file(&self.pid_file)` when the guard is destroyed. No validation ties this path to `pid_path()` or the state directory. Thus any daemon subprocess reaching `from_env()` and then dropping the guard deletes an attacker-selected file path reachable by that process.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Ignore env path; recompute PID path internally or validate it stays under state_dir().

proposed_findings.title: Daemon writes PID and log files through attacker-controlled HOME
preconditions: Attacker can set `HOME` before invoking the daemon
proof: `state_dir()` builds `~/.hf-mount` directly from `std::env::var_os("HOME")`, else `/tmp`. `pid_path()` and `log_path()` append attacker-influenced filenames there, and `daemonize()` calls `create_dir_all`, opens the log with `.create(true).append(true)`, and writes the PID file. No validation or trusted directory lookup constrains `HOME`, so starting the daemon writes files under any user-chosen path reachable by the process.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Use a trusted home/state directory source; reject or ignore untrusted `HOME` for daemon files.

proposed_findings.title: Read-only mode still accepts mutating NFS RPCs
preconditions: NFS server mounted with `read_only=true`
proof: `mount_nfs` passes `read_only` into `NFSAdapter::new`; `capabilities()` then only returns `VFSCapabilities::ReadOnly`. But mutating handlers `setattr`, `write`, `create`, `create_exclusive`, `mkdir`, `remove`, `rename`, and `symlink` never check `self.read_only` and directly call `virtual_fs` mutation methods. Thus any client that sends those RPCs reaches backend state changes despite read-only mode, enabling unauthorized filesystem modification.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Reject every mutating RPC with `NFS3ERR_ROFS` when `self.read_only` is true.

proposed_findings.title: Client-supplied uid/gid are applied without adapter-side checks
preconditions: Client can issue NFS `SETATTR` with uid/gid fields
proof: NFS request data enters `NFSAdapter::setattr` as `sattr3`. At `src/nfs.rs:213`, `setattr.uid` and `setattr.gid` are decoded directly into `Some(u)`/`Some(g)` and passed unchanged to `self.virtual_fs.setattr(id, size, mode, uid, gid, atime, mtime)`. No adapter-side permission, identity, or value checks occur before crossing into `virtual_fs`. Thus any reachable `SETATTR` call can request ownership changes using client-supplied uid/gid values.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Reject client uid/gid changes here, or enforce caller authorization before forwarding.

proposed_findings.title: NFS create honors untrusted uid/gid fields
preconditions: Writable NFS client can send CREATE with uid/gid attributes
proof: `create` reads `attr.uid`/`attr.gid` from client-supplied `sattr3` and, when present, assigns them directly to `uid`/`gid` in `src/nfs.rs:261`. It then calls `create_file`, which forwards them unchanged to `virtual_fs.create(dirid, name, mode, uid, gid, None)`. No validation or remapping appears on this path. A reachable CREATE request can therefore choose persisted file ownership metadata instead of server defaults.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Ignore client uid/gid on create; always use server-derived defaults or authenticated identity mapping.

proposed_findings.title: Staging directory creation panics on filesystem errors
preconditions: Attacker influences `cache_dir` to an uncreatable path
proof: `StagingDir::new` takes caller-provided `cache_dir`, joins `staging`, then calls `std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap_or_else(...)` in `src/xet.rs:173`. Any filesystem error creating that path triggers the panic path instead of returning `Result`. This is directly reachable whenever staging is initialized with an invalid or inaccessible cache directory, causing process abort/denial of service rather than recoverable error handling.
proposed_findings.fix_outline: Make `StagingDir::new` return `Result<Self>` and propagate `create_dir_all` failures as `Error`.

proposed_findings.title: Bounded download range lacks local ordering validation
preconditions: Caller can pass `end: Some(u64)` to bounded download
proof: `download_stream` accepts caller-provided `offset` and `end` and, in the `Some(end)` branch, directly builds `FileRange::new(offset, end)` at `src/xet.rs:88` with no `end >= offset` check. The documented contract expects `[offset, end)`, so `end < offset` violates local range ordering before handing control to `FileReconstructor`. This reachable malformed range can trigger incorrect bounded-download behavior or downstream errors.

finding.title: Untrusted args file controls mount configuration
preconditions: attacker can write shared `tmp_dir` volume args file
proof: Input originates from `tmp_dir/.volumes/*/args`, described as a shared emptyDir. `discover_pending()` reads each file with `read_to_string`, splits lines into tokens, and passes them directly to `MountArgs::try_parse_from`, then `run_mount()` uses the parsed `source` and `options` in `build()`. No check binds files to the CSI driver or validates ownership/source. Any writer to the shared directory can influence mount configuration for a launched mount.
finding.fix_outline: Verify args file provenance before parsing, e.g. trusted ownership/path checks or authenticated driver-signed configs.
